sections.h2: What is the first thing to know about selling a house in Westland?
sections.html:
Westland requires a Certificate of Approval on every house sold or transferred, and it has to be in place before the residential sale closes. That rule shapes the whole timeline, so it comes ahead of price, repairs or buyer choice. The city's Building Division runs the process, and the seller normally starts it.

Westland sits in Wayne County about 18 miles west of downtown Detroit. Deeds for Westland houses are recorded with the Wayne County Register of Deeds, and the county's rules on appointments, fees and tax certification are different from neighboring Macomb or Kent counties.

sections.h2: How did Westland grow into the city it is now?
sections.html:
Westland was part of Nankin Township until residents voted on May 16, 1966 to form a city. The township had grown to about 70,000 people by 1960, which made it the largest township in the state, and the vote was a response to Livonia's attempts to annex the land where the Westland Shopping Center was being built. That mall opened in 1965.

The Norwayne subdivision is among the oldest parts of the city. It went up right after World War II as temporary housing for returning soldiers who worked in nearby factories. The city covers 20.4 square miles, and the population has stayed between about 84,000 and 87,000 at every census since 1970.

Ford Road (M-153) runs through central Westland. Hines Park, a Wayne County park, runs through the northern part of the city, and the city also runs its own neighborhood parks. Trash pickup is weekly in black bins, and blue recycling bins are collected every other week.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Westland addresses?
sections.html:
Most of Westland belongs to the Wayne-Westland Community School District. John Glenn High School serves central and parts of northern Westland, while students in parts of southern Westland attend Wayne Memorial High School in the neighboring city of Wayne. The northernmost part of the city is in Livonia Public Schools, with Livonia's Churchill and Franklin high schools.

A few corners of southeastern Westland are split between Romulus Community Schools and the Taylor School District, a result of the Inkster district's dissolution. Since the line can change from one block to the next, ask the district for the assignment tied to the street address, and tell the buyer which district applies.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show for Westland homeowners?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 82,333 people, a 3.6 percent decline from the 2020 base of 85,409. The 2020 count found 39,633 housing units with 4.9 percent vacant. The bureau's 2020 through 2024 figures show 35,932 households of 2.30 people each.

Only 61.3 percent of Westland homes are owner-occupied, a lower share than many Michigan suburbs, so rental registration matters more here. The median owner-occupied home is valued at $184,600, median rent is $1,158 and median household income is $62,076. Owner costs with a mortgage have a median of $1,360 a month.

sections.h2: How does Westland's Certificate of Approval work?
sections.html:
The seller files a Home Sale or Transfer application with the Building Division, which is at 36300 Warren Road, phone 734-467-3210, open Monday through Friday from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. A housing inspector then checks the house against the property maintenance code. The seller can ask for an inspection online, by email at building@cityofwestland.com, by phone or in person.

  • The furnace or boiler must be tested and certified on the city's own form by a mechanical contractor registered with Westland.
  • A house with a fireplace also needs a safety inspection report from a chimney contractor.
  • When the seller passes, the Certificate of Approval is good for six months.
  • If the seller does not finish, the buyer can purchase an Approval Letter to Close, return a Remaining Violations Disclosure Form with the signed purchase agreement, and then has ninety days to repair and schedule the final inspection.

The second route can suit an as-is cash purchase: the sale closes with the open items, and the buyer takes on the repairs afterward.

sections.h2: Do open permits or rentals complicate a Westland sale?
sections.html:
They can. The Building Division issues the permits that homeowners most often skip: re-roofing, decks, fences, fireplaces, garages, pools, kitchen expansions and basement finishing all need one, and electrical, plumbing and heating work each take a separate trade permit. A housing inspector walking the house for the Certificate of Approval is likely to ask about any of that work, so gather permit numbers and final approvals before the visit.

Westland also runs a rental program, with a Rental Registration Application on the Building Division's forms list. An owner selling a tenant-occupied house should ask the Building Division at 734-467-3210 how the registration and the sale certificate interact, and whether the rental registration is current before the house goes under contract.

Westland's Planning and Building Department also lists a Temporary Certificate of Occupancy request form, a separate route used while work is still unfinished. Ask the department whether that form applies to your situation before you promise a buyer a closing date.

sections.h2: What does a Westland sale cost in city and county charges?
sections.html:
The city fee depends on the building type. The county records the deed for $30 per document ($26 plus the $4 state survey fee) under a schedule that took effect January 1, 2026, the first increase at that office since 1996. Wayne County also requires the county treasurer's tax certification on deeds and land contracts unless an exemption applies.

sections.h2: How do I record a deed with the Wayne County Register of Deeds?
sections.html:
Since October 1, 2025 the office serves customers by appointment only. A person recording up to five documents books a 20 minute slot, and the 45 minute slots are reserved for people recording five to 25 documents. The scheduling line is 313-224-5860, and the recording help line is 313-224-5851.

The county lists these common reasons a deed is returned:

  • A copied signature instead of an original.
  • No consideration amount or exemption statute cited on the deed.
  • First page without a 2.5 inch top margin, or text under 10 point.
  • The first five digits of a Social Security number left visible.
  • No county treasurer tax certification on a warranty deed.

Transfer tax must be paid in cash, check or money order. The office also accepts credit and debit cards with matching ID, but not American Express or Discover. A check more than $25 over the amount due is returned unprocessed.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Westland house without a Certificate of Approval?
faqs.a: Yes, in one case. If the seller does not finish the inspection, the buyer purchases an Approval Letter to Close for $80 and signs the violations disclosure form. The buyer then has ninety days to complete the repairs and pass the final inspection.

faqs.q: How much is the Westland Home Sale or Transfer fee?
faqs.a: It is $250 for a single-family house, $475 for a duplex and $900 for a multi-family building, according to the city's Rev. 7-1-26 application. The seller files it with the Building Division.

faqs.q: How long does a Westland Certificate of Approval last?
faqs.a: It lasts six months from the date it is issued to a seller who completes the inspection. The furnace certification form must be on file before the Building Division grants final approval.

faqs.q: Who pays Michigan transfer tax on a Westland sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it under the state transfer tax acts. Wayne County prints the rates as $0.55 per $500 for the county and $3.75 per $500 for the state, collected when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Do I need an appointment to record a deed for a Westland house?
faqs.a: Yes. The Wayne County Register of Deeds has required appointments since October 1, 2025, with the first slot at 8:00 a.m. and the last at 3:50 p.m. Ask the Westland Finance Department for property tax amounts and due dates before closing.
